subject: HelioHealth — request for one-time commercial concession & VPC surcharge waiver (VP/CFO signoff)
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: HelioHealth one-time concession + VPC surcharge waiver

Team — quick ask. HelioHealth (prospect -> strategic pilot) has asked for a one-time commercial concession: 35% off list for the first 12 months and a waiver of the $15k one-time VPC / setup surcharge. Rationale: they are a regulated payer that is willing to (a) sign a 12-month committed pilot, (b) include Redwood as a preferred inference vendor for their internal AI roadmap, and (c) provide a joint case study post-pilot.

Snapshot:
- Estimated ARR run-rate if pilot converts: ~$420k/year (year-1 blended)
- Pilot ARR (committed monthly minimum): ~$28k/mo for 12 months
- Usage profile: steady RL inference for clinical triage, expected 60M tokens/mo during pilot peak (we have initial telemetry)
- They require a private VPC deployment (data residency + SOC2 controls) — hence the one-time setup surcharge ask

Commercial ask: 35% off list for year-1 + waive the one-time $15k VPC charge. We can tie the concession to: signed 12-month term, no logo/public case study without approval, and a one-time executive sponsor commitment from the customer.

Why escalate: projected revenue impact >$90k ARR vs standard pricing and the VPC waiver is outside standard packaging. Marcus endorses but says we need VP/CFO signoff.

Attachments: HelioHealth-Quote-v3.pdf; HelioHealth-MAP_v2.xlsx (usage + forecast).

Next steps I need from finance/legal:
- Kimberly: can you weigh in on the total credit cap and whether we can approve the waiver?
- Marissa: would you and Finance consider conditional signoff, or should we route to CFO?

I can loop procurement/legal if you want the customer-facing redline before sign. I flagged deal HLH-2026-1123 in HubSpot.

Thanks — Jonas
--
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: HelioHealth one-time concession + VPC surcharge waiver

Thanks Jonas — a few clarifying items before I can greenlight anything to VP/CFO:

1) ARR impact calc: can you confirm the net revenue delta versus standard pricing across the 12-month period (include token-based overage exposure)?
2) Are we comfortable with the case study conditionality? We generally prefer a public mention clause tied to marketing approval; fine to keep it conditional.
3) Can Legal confirm there are no unusual indemnities tied to the private deployment (I see HelioHealth's standard legal asks in the HubSpot doc).
4) Can we propose an upper bound on total credits/discount dollars (e.g., limit to $100k one-time equivalent) so accounting can model worst-case?

If we can cap the exposure and get Legal to approve the standard SOW redlines, I'd be inclined to recommend to Marissa that we approve a concession, but likely smaller than 35% unless execs want to trade other levers (e.g., a multi-year commit or prepayment).

Please attach the ARR delta table (or paste numbers inline) and confirm whether the customer is open to a 12-month term + optional auto-renew.

Kimberly
--
Kimberly Park
Director, Finance (Commercial)
kimberly_park@redwood.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 14:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: HelioHealth one-time concession + VPC surcharge waiver

Kimberly — answers inline and attached small ARR workbook (see HelioHealth-MAP_v2.xlsx):

1) Net delta vs standard price: with 35% concession, year-1 recognized revenue declines by ~$95,000 vs list (we modeled token-based overages at conservative 20% headroom). Worst-case total credits (discount on usage + waived VPC) = ~$110k.
2) Case study: customer agreed to an "approved case study" clause — Marketing will get final sign-off; they asked for a marketing timeline post-pilot.
3) Legal asks: standard HelioHealth redlines look normal; they requested a data processing addendum and slightly longer indemnity windows. Procurement will accept our standard DPA with a few clarifying amendments.
4) Cap proposal: we can cap the concession exposure to $110k (which is aligned with the 35% ask). Alternatively, if Finance/Leadership prefers a smaller hit, I can offer 25% in return for a 24-month commit and a $50k prepayment.

Customer context: Anna Patel (Head of AI) is driving this and procurement is receptive to the 12-month minimum. Deal ID HLH-2026-1123 in HubSpot.

Recommend: Finance and Leadership decide between (A) 35% + VPC waiver capped at $110k for a 12-month pilot (exec sponsor + approved case study), or (B) 25% + VPC fee waived contingent on 24-month commit + $50k prepayment.

I will push the alternative (B) in our next customer conversation if leadership wants a smaller concession.

-Jonas

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 11:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: HelioHealth one-time concession + VPC surcharge waiver

Quick take from Sales leadership: I support a concession to win this pilot — HelioHealth is a strategic prospect in payer space with potential to expand across multiple lines if the pilot succeeds. That said, given the ~$110k downside, we should aim to reduce that exposure if Finance prefers.

If Marissa is comfortable, I'd recommend signoff at 30% + VPC waiver, capped at $90k, with the following mandatory commercial protections:
- 12-month minimum term + executive sponsor from customer
- Usage-based overage pricing preserved beyond committed minimum
- Marketing/case study approvals explicitly controlled by us

If Leadership wants to tighten further, Jonas can present the 25%/24-month/prepay alternative to the customer.

Marcus
--
Marcus Lin
Head of Sales, West Region
marcus_lin@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 07 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: HelioHealth one-time concession + VPC surcharge waiver

Thanks for the clear framing. After reviewing numbers and risk, I'm prepared to provide conditional VP/CFO signoff with the following constraints:

1) Approved concession: 30% off list for year-1 (not the full 35%).
2) Waive the $15k one-time VPC setup fee.
3) Concession exposure cap: $90,000 total (discount + waived fee).
4) Required customer commitments: signed 12-month minimum term, executive sponsor assigned, and our approved marketing clause to govern any case study.
5) Legal: finalize DPA and accept limited indemnity language — attach redline back to me before sending to customer.

If Finance wants to tighten (e.g., require prepayment or 24-month commit), I'm okay routing back to CFO, but for speed of conversion I'd approve the above. Marcus/Jonas: proceed to update the quote and ask the customer to sign the amended SOW.

Marissa
